Use the controls

Native240×240. The LCD is not a touch control. Text on this page explains the model; it is not added to the firmware screen.

Pads use press/release timing, including pointer capture and keyboard press/release. The named hold fixture remains a controlled input. Turn counts are logical gestures, not measured encoder detents. The ordinary arrow press route is available; menu hold-repeat, simultaneous arrows and held-FX/connected ownership are not qualified. ARP and FADER BANK remain visible but disabled because their model routes are unfinished. Only proposal note/motion data changes; no firmware audio or storage runs.

37 physical key inputs

These inputs use physical indices0–36 and the source keyboard admission rules. PART or SEQ Free Play with REC off admits37; current REC uses the central27. Stopped REC replaces visited cells at V100; this is current policy, not a new take object or selected future capture strategy. Printed controller octaves and stored/displayed MIDI pitches remain distinct.

Normal X0X controls ·27-key logical surface

The37-key hardware is C3–C6. Legacy X0X control roles use F3–G5:16 white and11 black keys. The separate admitted live synth route uses all37 in PART or SEQ Free Play with REC off. Clip keyboard also uses all37; no keybed LEDs exist. This inspection model uses the normal GRID mapping.

Eleven physical black keys · contextual track selection

These controls identify physical key inputs. Highlight is a model selection marker, not a physical keybed light. The SMK keybed has no LEDs.

Sixteen physical RGB pads · GRID fixture

No calibrated percentage or charging line is exposed. The requested percentage-inside-glyph needs a validated data contract; bars are not converted into false percentages.

Normal pads keep the selected part hue. Content/playhead inversion and held-input priority are retained. Mute identity stays on the LCD; no new mute/held/REC pad colour is invented. Browser colour is not measured hardware brightness. Button outlines denote source on/off, not an invented RGB button.
